sections.overview: Cirrhoscyllium japonicum is a small carpet shark of the Northwest Pacific, endemic to southern Japan.
sections.identification: It has dark saddle-like markings and a pair of throat barbels; adults remain much smaller than large reef-associated carpet sharks.
sections.habitat: The IUCN account describes a demersal shelf shark from shallow water to about 200 m, while Okinawa aquarium observations document individuals near 400 m locally.
sections.diet: Its diet has not been characterized in the sources consulted.
sections.behavior: An Okinawa aquarium account describes it as mostly sedentary and not an active swimmer, while wild behavioral observations remain limited.
sections.reproduction: It is oviparous; the aquarium reported two eggs from a captive female and successful hatching, but this is an observation rather than a population-wide breeding estimate.
sections.ecology: It is one of three Cirrhoscyllium species; its saddle pattern and Japanese records distinguish it from the Taiwan-restricted C. formosanum and South China Sea C. expolitum.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern with a stable trend, but species-level biological information remains limited.
